about_the_game:
The Dinner – DEMO

Step inside. Follow the routine. Try to keep your mind intact.

This short playable demo offers a 15–20 minute experience of The Dinner, a narrative-driven psychological horror game set in a deceptively peaceful 1950s home.

You wake up alone. Your wife, Emma, is out.

What to Expect in the Demo:

  • Everyday Tasks, Unsettling Atmosphere
    Complete mundane chores in a mid-century home… while unease simmers beneath the surface.

  • Hallucinations That Twist Reality
    The house distorts around you—shadows flicker, voices whisper, and reality fractures. Suppress the visions with pills or vinyl records.

  • Subtle Storytelling
    Uncover fragments of a bigger mystery through environmental storytelling and the protagonist’s internal monologue. Nothing is explained outright—everything is implied.

  • Music as a Lifeline
    Sound becomes your defense against the overwhelming chaos of your mind. But silence always returns.

This demo is a small taste of the full game, focusing on mood, tension, and fragmented memory. It does not feature the complete narrative or all mechanics from the final version. Instead, it introduces you to the world of The Dinner—where not even your own mind can be trusted.

How long can you hold on before reality slips away?

Mature Content Description

This game contains intense psychological horror themes, depictions of PTSD, hallucinations, and unsettling imagery. There are sequences of paranoia behavior, including mentions of substance dependency (medication) to manage mental health issues. Players sensitive to themes of psychological distress, war trauma, or violence should be advised.

short_description: In 1950, a war veteran living in a house that should feel like home is haunted by eerie hallucinations and a suffocating sense of dread, and must fight to keep his sanity intact. The horror is more real than it seems...
